content.text: The text surveys German responses to Laurence Sterne, especially sentimental travel narratives by Jacobi, Schummel, Bock, Göchhausen, Wezel, and others. It distinguishes genuine sympathy from affected “Empfindelei,” discusses imitation of Sterne’s plots, characters, digressions, typography, and animal sentiment, and describes criticism by Goethe, Lichtenberg, Campe, Timme, and others. Later material shifts abruptly to advertisements, agricultural news, market reports, humor, fiction, and a girl’s diary. The diary records visits and journeys to Victor, Penn Yan, Le Roy, Utica, Clinton, Canandaigua, Litchfield, Farmington, Hartford, New York, and Havana-related experiences; it also describes churches, homes, schools, cemeteries, theaters, banks, farms, and other specific places.
